letter: You answered every ask in the first round, so most of this one is Claude's to carry out, not yours to read. The Library's shape is settled and its close-ups can start; the animation work goes into the app next; the desk is now the way questions reach you, written into how every session works. One thing is genuinely yours, and it's the one you asked for: Lumi's proposed behaviour, as claims to keep or strike. Two things wait on your hands because they're your accounts. Everything else below is just so you can see it.

asks.title: Lumi's proposed behaviour: thirteen claims to keep or strike
asks.context: You asked for this shape last round. Everything in `lumi.md` marked *proposed* is Claude's draft, not canon — behaviour the persona partly implements but nobody has agreed to. It's now thirteen short claims. What you keep becomes canon and the persona has to match it; what you strike is deleted, so it can't quietly come back.
points: 1 · The drift tells: how we'd notice her becoming a nagging coach, a reminder system, a taskmaster, a sycophant, a faux therapist, an optimiser or a quote generator.
2 · Needs to think it through: reflection that moves toward a choice, never a task list or premature steps.
3 · Circling: when the same worry returns with nothing new, she names the loop gently and offers one step.
4 · Avoidance vs reprioritisation is a question of choice; a thing that drifts gets one curious question, asked once.
5 · Reflection is useful while it produces something; she moves in on a real question and back out when it stops.
6 · What she knows is used only when it changes what she'd say, woven in, never recited back.
8 · Before any line she starts: something changed, silence would cost something real, and it can be ignored at no cost.
9 · She challenges the frame, not the person — once, with a reason, then drops it.
10 · The tells of saccharine: reassurance before doubt, praise for ordinary things, a line that would fit anyone.
11 · A reading about the person is offered as a question; logistics are asserted. High stakes make the guess visible.
12 · Thinking out loud is not an instruction: she acts on nothing.
13 · Thinking something through has an exit: reflection produces a choice, then she steps back out.
asks.recommendation: Keep all thirteen. They're drawn from the vision and the principles, and the ones that aren't already in the persona are where she's thinnest. If any is wrong, name its number in your own words and it's struck — deleted from `lumi.md`, with this page recording that you struck it.
asks.ifSilent: They stay proposed, which is what they are today. Nothing becomes canon, and nothing regresses by waiting.

asks.title: Today at a glance: does the Garden's "one thing should dominate" become "one thing leads"?
asks.context: You asked for Today to focus less on breaking down one task and more on the day at a glance (2026-09-18). It's built on `ux/today-at-a-glance`: one sheet with Right now, After that, Later, Done today and the closing line. Right now is first and a size up, but it no longer takes the page. The Garden canon (§4) still says one thing should dominate, so the page and the canon now disagree.
points: Soften §4 to "one thing leads": the day reads at a glance, and the first thing on it is still the one to start with.
Keep §4 as written: the page comes back toward one dominant thing once you've lived with the glance.
asks.recommendation: Soften §4 to "one thing leads", with the one-second test kept: Right now stays first under its own kicker, and nothing past After that is shown. The path's curation still does the executive-function work; only the weight between its parts changes.
asks.ifSilent: The page stays as built and §4 stays as written, with the disagreement recorded in the product decisions. Nothing regresses by waiting.

compass.question: Does this reduce the user's executive-function burden, or accidentally create more of it?
principles: Lumi proposes, the user corrects, Lumi learns
Show less than you know; one decision at a time
Resistance and capacity change the plan
Appropriate forward movement, not maximum output
Show inference for what it is

learned: You answered all six asks with *Go with that* and wrote nothing extra, which is what a recommendation is for — but it also means the desk has no correction to learn from yet.

An ask can go stale while it sits here. The design notebook was tried, landed and pushed by another session on the day you were reading an ask that still called it unlanded. The desk only knows what it has swept.
One ask asked your permission for something Claude can't do: the Drive package needs a write path, not a yes. A recommendation has to be something Claude can actually carry out.
changing: The desk sweeps every merge since its last round before it renders, so an ask whose subject has already landed is retired instead of shown.
Seven asks last round, one this round. Four of last round's became delegations or settled direction, which is the desk working as intended.
Before an ask is written, Claude checks it is actually Claude's to carry out. If the block is a tool or a permission, it goes to *your hands* with the steps, not to you as a question.

forCoherence.lesson: Suggested answers are a floor, not a fence.
forCoherence.inApp: Wherever Lumi offers choices (*Not this*, the capacity question), plain words stay one step away, never hidden.
Lumi reconciles, not only remembers: something settled in one conversation quietly stops being open everywhere else.

forCoherence.lesson: Offer a proposal, not a question.
forCoherence.inApp: When starting is hard, the first step comes as something to say yes to, never *What do you want to do?*
Anything Lumi asks carries its default, so an unanswered question is never waiting for someone who comes back.

forCoherence.lesson: Let *you decide* teach, then confirm once.
forCoherence.inApp: A repeated *you pick* in one area becomes an offer of scoped authority, granted in conversation, never a setting.
*I'll hold this; you don't need to* is containment the user can trust.

forCoherence.lesson: Effort filters better than priority when tired.
forCoherence.inApp: Today's capacity answer could choose which kind of first step to offer, as well as how many.

forCoherence.lesson: Something answered elsewhere must stop being open here.
forCoherence.inApp: A thing the user settles in conversation quietly closes wherever else it was waiting — they never answer the same question twice because two parts of the system hadn't spoken.

forCoherence.lesson: Never ask for permission you can't act on.
forCoherence.inApp: Lumi doesn't ask the user to approve something she has no way to do; she says what she needs, or asks for the one step only they can take.
